risks.description: If any workflow state still lives only in an in-process cache, a process restart reverts to the last durably-written state, silently losing transitions the operator already saw applied.
risks.basis: AC 'workflow state survives a process restart'; unit U-P5-1 moves state from an in-process cache to the durable store.

risks.description: Rebuilding workflow/effect state from the persisted history on restart could re-drive an already-completed effect (double invoice / double commit) if a committed grant is treated as re-claimable.
risks.basis: AC 'rebuilding state from history never re-executes an effect'; checkpoint.py crash semantics: crash-after-commit -> grant EXPIRES unclaimed, re-checkpoint mints a NEW grant under the same commit_key.

risks.description: A write that fails partway (transition UPDATE matches !=1 rows, FK violation, integrity error) could leave a workflow run or grant in a half-applied state instead of rolling back cleanly.
risks.basis: AC 'a failed write leaves no partially applied workflow'; workflow.transition/_require_one_row rollback paths and _write_txn BEGIN IMMEDIATE.

risks.description: A read served from a stale in-process cache after a durable write would show the operator an old state (UI/backend disagreement).
risks.basis: AC 'a read after a write never returns stale state'; action_callback opens a fresh WorkflowStore per request (lines 320/368).

risks.description: The live-hold uniqueness (at most one GRANTED/CLAIMED/ATTEMPTED/VERIFIED/UNKNOWN_OUTCOME grant per (tenant,commit_key)) could be violated by the state-move change, permitting two live reservations for one logical effect.
risks.basis: migrations/phase3_checkpoint.py ix_effect_grants_live_hold partial unique index; workflow.operation_commit_claim raises on >1 live row.

risks.description: The checkpoint_witnesses append-only history could become mutable (missing triggers) or lose 1:1 witness:grant correspondence, corrupting the history that restart rebuilds from.
risks.basis: phase3_checkpoint.P3_TRIGGERS append-only triggers; checkpoint_witnesses UNIQUE(tenant,grant_id) FK to effect_grants.

risks.description: The cache->store move could regress the 22 tenant-scoped store methods or cross-tenant isolation guarantees.
risks.basis: workflow.py WorkflowStore tenant-first invariants; broad canonical suite.

scenarios.title: Durable workflow store survives a callback process restart
scenarios.purpose: Prove the workflow state lives in the durable store on disk (readable while the process is down and after it restarts), not in an in-process cache that a restart would drop.
scenarios.requirement_reference: workflow state survives a process restart
scenarios.isolation_note: Only stops/starts the callback service and reads the store; performs no writes to persisted rows, so it cannot contaminate other scenarios' data. Must not run concurrently with any scenario reading/writing the same driver_probe workflow.sqlite3.
setup: The callback service is running against data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3 with its canonical/P3 schema applied.
scenarios.rationale: The unit's whole point is that state is no longer process-local. Stopping the service and reading the same durable file, then restarting and re-opening it, is the direct observable of durability across a restart. A fresh WorkflowStore is opened per request, so a successful post-restart request also proves the process re-attaches to the durable store rather than an empty cache.

state_check.command: sqlite3 data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3 "SELECT 'PARTIAL:'||id FROM workflow_runs WHERE state IS NULL OR created_at IS NULL OR updated_at IS NULL"

expected_observations: The workflow_runs count is readable from the on-disk store before, during (service stopped), and after the restart.
After restart the service serves the callback path (400 for a missing token) by opening the durable store.
No workflow run is left in a partial (NULL state/created_at/updated_at) shape after restart.
forbidden_observations: 'no such table: workflow_runs' or a malformed/corrupt database while the service is stopped.
The service failing to answer /email/action after restart.
cleanup: Ensure the callback service is left running: start_service callback if it is down.

scenarios.title: Crash/restart matrix never re-executes a committed effect
scenarios.purpose: Exercise the constitutional crash matrix: crash-after-commit expires the grant unclaimed and a re-checkpoint mints a NEW grant under the same commit key without re-driving the effect.
scenarios.requirement_reference: rebuilding state from history never re-executes an effect
scenarios.isolation_note: Runs the checkpoint matrix test suite against its own temporary databases; touches no shared driver_probe state.
setup: The canonical test environment is installed (.venv present).
scenarios.rationale: test_phase3_checkpoint_matrix.py is the harness's deterministic encoding of the 105-case oracle including crash-after-commit and re-mint safety, which is exactly 'rebuilding state from history never re-executes an effect'. A green run is strong, reproducible evidence for the highest-weight AC.
expected_observations: The checkpoint matrix suite passes, exit code 0.
forbidden_observations: Any failing/errored case in the crash or re-mint rows of the matrix.

scenarios.title: Witness is single-use and the claim CAS admits exactly one claim
scenarios.purpose: Confirm a checkpoint witness authorizes exactly one mint and the GRANTED->CLAIMED compare-and-set is single-serialization, so a replay/rebuild cannot produce a second effect.
scenarios.requirement_reference: rebuilding state from history never re-executes an effect
scenarios.isolation_note: Runs witness and claim-CAS tests against their own temporary databases; no shared state touched.
setup: The canonical test environment is installed (.venv present).
scenarios.rationale: claim_grant_cas is the sole serialization point of the effect (zero rows updated => caller does nothing). These suites prove single-use witness and single-claim CAS directly, which is the mechanism that makes replay-on-rebuild non-executing.
expected_observations: Both witness and claim-CAS suites pass, exit code 0.
forbidden_observations: A witness minting two grants or a grant admitting two claims.

scenarios.title: At most one live-hold grant per (tenant, commit_key) in the durable ledger
scenarios.purpose: Guard the live-hold uniqueness invariant on the real dogfood store: no logical effect may hold two simultaneous live reservations, which would enable a double external effect after a rebuild.
scenarios.requirement_reference: a failed write leaves no partially applied workflow
scenarios.isolation_note: Read-only SELECT against the persisted store; performs no writes. Must not run concurrently with S1 (restart) on the same DB.
setup: The callback service's durable store exists at data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3.
scenarios.rationale: operation_commit_claim raises if it ever sees more than one live row; this state_check asserts the same invariant holds in the actual persisted ledger, independent of the temp DBs the unit tests use. On an empty ledger it is a vacuous guard, but it can only ever surface a real violation.

state_check.command: sqlite3 data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3 "SELECT 'VIOLATION:'||tenant||'/'||commit_key||'='||count(*) FROM effect_grants WHERE state IN ('GRANTED','CLAIMED','ATTEMPTED','VERIFIED','UNKNOWN_OUTCOME') GROUP BY tenant,commit_key HAVING count(*)>1"

expected_observations: No (tenant, commit_key) has more than one live-hold grant row.

scenarios.title: Witness history is append-only and 1:1 with its grant
scenarios.purpose: Confirm the immutable-history invariant that restart rebuilds from: append-only triggers present and every witness maps to exactly one grant.
scenarios.requirement_reference: rebuilding state from history never re-executes an effect
scenarios.isolation_note: Read-only SELECTs against the persisted store; no writes. Must not run concurrently with S1 on the same DB.
setup: The durable store at data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3 has the P3 schema applied.
scenarios.rationale: If the history the rebuild reads can be mutated (triggers dropped) or a witness can float without its grant, the reconstruction that must never re-execute an effect is built on corruptible evidence. This asserts both structural guarantees on the real store.

state_check.command: sqlite3 data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3 "SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='trigger' AND name LIKE 'trg_checkpoint_witnesses_append_only%'"

sqlite3 data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3 "SELECT 'ORPHAN:'||w.checkpoint_id FROM checkpoint_witnesses w LEFT JOIN effect_grants g ON w.tenant=g.tenant AND w.grant_id=g.grant_id WHERE g.grant_id IS NULL"

expected_observations: Both append-only triggers exist on checkpoint_witnesses.
No witness row references a missing grant.

scenarios.title: Canonical schema provides a durable home for all workflow state
scenarios.purpose: Verify the canonical schema builds every table the durable workflow state depends on, so there is somewhere durable for state to live after the move off the in-process cache.
scenarios.requirement_reference: workflow state survives a process restart
scenarios.isolation_note: Builds a schema in a throwaway tempdir via the approved probe; no shared state touched.
setup: The canonical test environment is installed (.venv present).
scenarios.rationale: A cheap, deterministic confirmation that create_canonical_schema materializes the durable tables (workflow_runs, audit_events, effect_grants, checkpoint_witnesses, brakes, platform_brake). If a table the state-move relies on is absent, durability across restart is impossible.

actions.name: canonical-schema-tables
actions.command: .venv/bin/python -c "import sqlite3,tempfile,os,sys; sys.path.insert(0,'src'); from freight_recon.schema import create_canonical_schema; p=os.path.join(tempfile.mkdtemp(),'probe.sqlite3'); c=sqlite3.connect(p); create_canonical_schema(c); print(sorted(r[0] for r in c.execute(\"select name from sqlite_master where type='table'\")))"

expected_observations: The printed table list contains all durable workflow/effect/witness tables.
forbidden_observations: Any of the required tables missing from the printed list.

scenarios.title: Full canonical suite: no partial-write / stale-read / tenant regressions
scenarios.purpose: Run the whole canonical suite as the backstop for the failed-write-atomicity and read-after-write ACs and to catch any regression the state-move introduced across the 22 tenant-scoped store methods.
scenarios.requirement_reference: a failed write leaves no partially applied workflow
scenarios.isolation_note: Runs the suite against its own temporary databases; no shared driver_probe state touched.
setup: The canonical test environment is installed (.venv present).
scenarios.rationale: transition()/_require_one_row rollback-on-rowcount!=1 and the WAL/BEGIN-IMMEDIATE atomicity are exercised by the suite; a full green run is the honest backstop for AC #2 (no partial write) and AC #3 (no stale read) which cannot be independently driven at the HTTP layer without a signed token.
expected_observations: The full canonical suite passes, exit code 0.
forbidden_observations: Any failing test in the workflow-store, transition-atomicity, or tenant-isolation areas.

scenarios.title: Durable store is configured for fresh cross-connection reads (WAL)
scenarios.purpose: Confirm the persisted store uses WAL so a reader on a new connection sees the latest committed write — the mechanism that prevents a read from returning stale (formerly cached) state.
scenarios.requirement_reference: a read after a write never returns stale state
scenarios.isolation_note: Read-only PRAGMA/SELECT against the persisted store; no writes. Must not run concurrently with S1 on the same DB.
setup: The callback service has opened data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3 at least once (WAL mode is set at store construction).
scenarios.rationale: The callback opens a fresh WorkflowStore per request, so freshness depends on each new connection reading the latest committed disk state; WAL is what guarantees a concurrent reader is not pinned to a stale snapshot. This checks the durable mechanism directly and asserts no run is left without a committed state.

state_check.command: sqlite3 data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3 "SELECT 'NOSTATE:'||id FROM workflow_runs WHERE state IS NULL"

expected_observations: No workflow run has a NULL state.
forbidden_observations: journal_mode reporting delete/rollback instead of wal.

unresolved_questions: I could not drive an end-to-end proof of the cache->store move at the HTTP layer: every state-changing callback route (/actions/signed, /email/action, /slack/*) requires a valid signed action token or Slack signature, and I may not use secrets, so I cannot create-then-restart-then-read a NEW workflow run through the running service. The restart evidence (S1) therefore asserts durability/integrity of the existing store across restart plus service recovery, not the survival of a specific transition applied via the API. Is there an approved, secret-free way to seed a workflow transition into the driver_probe store (e.g., a fixture loader) so a true before/after-restart state comparison can be authored?

State-of-the-store invariant checks (S4, S5, S8) are vacuous if the driver_probe ledger is empty at run time. Confirm whether the dogfood service is expected to have persisted runs/grants/witnesses when these scenarios run, or whether a seeding step should precede them.

The AC 'a read after a write never returns stale state' has no secret-free HTTP driver available to me; I approximated it with the WAL/per-connection freshness mechanism (S8) plus the full suite (S7). If there is an approved endpoint or script that performs a write and an immediately-following read against driver_probe, a stronger direct scenario could be authored.

The repository does not point me at the specific in-process cache being removed by U-P5-1 (no clearly-named cache module surfaced); scenarios are grounded in the durable WorkflowStore/ledger semantics the ACs describe rather than in the exact code path deleted. Confirm the source module/field that previously held the cached state.
